comments.author: einr
comments.why: Fun video explaining analog floppy-disk still cameras
comments.text: Yes, probably -- before digital cameras, there were still video cameras. They used a CCD to record still video images onto magnetic media such as a video floppy disk. So a lot like a digital camera, but fully analog. These were pretty cutting-edge tech in the mid 80's and would have made a lot of sense for a project like this. comments.author: qingcharles
comments.story: A 'toaster with a lens': The story behind the first handheld digital camera
comments.why: Related to the commenter's analog floppy Canon camera
comments.text: It's interesting that you differentiate between analog and digital electronic cameras. My first "digital" camera was one of the Canon Ion ones that use floppy discs but actually record the photos in analog, so technically just an "electronic camera", but was marketed as a "Still Video Camera" (!). You had to use a video capture card to get the images into the PC. [LINK] [VIDEO]

comments.author: gambiting
comments.story: A floppy-disk Walkman using a Raspberry Pi
comments.why: Example of cameras storing analog NTSC photos on floppies
comments.text: Similarly, there have been photo cameras that used floppies for image storage, and I'm not talking about sony's Cybershoot cameras which stored photos as actual files - I'm talking cameras which just stored photos as analog signal directly on the floppy, in NTSC format! [VIDEO]
